chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Muskān, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to dislike slaughter and the spilling of blood on Friday before the prayer, except out of necessity.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: The prayer (specifically the congregational Friday prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering animals on Friday before the congregational prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic preference (karāhah) against ritual slaughter on Friday prior to the congregational prayer, reflecting the desire to preserve the sanctity of the day for worship. The exception for necessity (ḍarūrah) aligns with general Islamic legal principles, ensuring that practical needs do not conflict with spiritual observance. This ruling is often discussed in the context of Friday's unique status as the 'chief of days' in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from one of our companions, from Abdullah Bin Muskaan, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to dislike the slaughter and spilling the blood on the day of Friday before the Prayer, except out of necessity’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa from al-‘ Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Marwak ibn ‘Ubayd from certain persons of our people from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, disliked slaughtering (animals) and spilling blood on Fridays before Salat (prayer) except in the case of an emergency.’”
